name: Pelvic Tilt (Cat/Cow)

execution.note: Focus on the tucking of the tailbone.

instructions: Step 1: Start on hands and knees with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips.
Step 2: Inhale, drop your belly toward the floor, and look up slightly (Cow).
Step 3: Exhale, round your spine toward the ceiling, and tuck your chin to your chest (Cat).
Step 4: Move rhythmically with your breath.

variations.name: Evening Pelvic Release Shake
variations.instruction_note: A loose, shaking movement on all fours to release evening tension.

variations.name: Quick Prep 8-Rep
variations.instruction_note: Perform exactly 8 reps as part of a 5-minute daily routine.

variations.name: Deep Belly Breath Focus
variations.instruction_note: Emphasize expanding the belly fully on the inhale.

variations.name: Feet In/Out Modification
variations.instruction_note: Experiment with bringing feet together or wide to change pelvic sensations.

safety_profile.trimester_3_notes: Very safe. If wrists are sore, perform on fists instead.

enrichment.benefits: Helps baby move into the optimal position (LOA) and relieves back pressure.

name: Forward-Leaning Inversion
instructions: Step 1: Kneel on the edge of a couch or stable chair.
Step 2: Carefully lower your hands to the floor one at a time, then lower onto your forearms.
Step 3: Let your head hang freely, tucking your chin slightly to create space in the neck.
Step 4: Keep your knees on the edge of the couch and hips high.
Step 5: To come out, crawl your hands back up to a kneeling position slowly.

variations.name: Doula Optimization Protocol
variations.instruction_note: Immediately follow the inversion with a period of rest or a gentle walk to help the baby settle into the newly created space.

variations.name: 3rd Trimester Low-Impact Version
variations.instruction_note: A slightly modified angle for very late pregnancy comfort.

safety_profile.trimester_3_notes: Always have someone nearby for balance if you feel unsteady. Come up very slowly to prevent a head rush.
safety_profile.contraindications: High blood pressure, history of stroke, glaucoma, or if baby is already in a perfect position and you are in active labor.

enrichment.benefits: Uses gravity to stretch the uterosacral ligaments, giving the baby more room to rotate into the optimal head-down position.

name: Hug the Baby (Pregnant Cat)

execution.note: Focus on the quality of the contraction rather than speed.

instructions: Step 1: Start on hands and knees with a neutral, flat spine.
Step 2: On the inhale, allow your stomach to expand fully toward the floor.
Step 3: On the exhale, blow all the air out and 'hug' your baby in and up toward your spine.
Step 4: Maintain a flat back; do not round your shoulders or tuck your tailbone.
Step 5: Feel the engagement of your deep transverse abdominis and your pelvic floor.

variations.name: Deep Belly Breathes
variations.instruction_note: Focus specifically on the diaphragmatic expansion to relax the pelvic floor on the inhale.

safety_profile.trimester_3_notes: Ensure you are not holding your breath. The engagement happens on the active exhale.
safety_profile.contraindications: Stop if you notice 'coning' or 'doming' along the center of your abdomen.

enrichment.benefits: Strengthens the transverse abdominis to support the weight of the belly and stabilize the spine.

name: Seated Hip Internal Rotation

execution.note: 10-25 reps per side, ideally performed morning and evening.

instructions: Step 1: Sit on the floor with your legs wide in a 'V' shape.
Step 2: Lean back slightly on your hands for support.
Step 3: Rotate one knee inward toward the floor, aiming for a 90-degree angle at the knee.
Step 4: Keep the other leg stable and the opposite hip grounded.
Step 5: Return to center and alternate sides.

variations.name: Deep Squat Internal Rotation
variations.instruction_note: Perform the rotation while staying in a deep squat position for added intensity.

variations.name: 90/90 Lift
variations.instruction_note: A strength-based variation where you lift the hip from a 90/90 seated position.

safety_profile.trimester_3_notes: Do not force the knee to the floor if you feel sharp pain. Only rotate within your comfortable range of motion.
safety_profile.contraindications: Sharp knee or hip joint pain.

enrichment.benefits: Increases the space in the lower pelvis (outlet), which is critical for the baby's exit during delivery.

name: Frog Pose Rocking

execution.note: Move rhythmically to help baby descend.

instructions: Step 1: Start on all fours and widen your knees as far as comfortable.
Step 2: Turn your toes outward so your inner feet are flat on the floor.
Step 3: Keep your forearms or hands on the floor for support.
Step 4: Slowly rock your hips back toward your heels and then forward again.

variations.name: Skeletal View Alignment
variations.instruction_note: Focus on the backward rock to specifically open the sit bones.

variations.name: Deep Hip Opening Hold
variations.instruction_note: A static version for deeper release of the pelvic floor.

variations.name: Quick Prep Variation
variations.instruction_note: Perform 8 rhythmic rocks as part of a high-efficiency circuit.

variations.name: Frogger Stretch
variations.instruction_note: Really focus on opening the hips wide to the sides.

safety_profile.trimester_3_notes: Use a blanket under your knees if the floor is too hard. Skip or narrow your knees if you feel sharp pain in the pubic bone (SPD).

enrichment.benefits: Creates space in the upper pelvis for the baby to drop down and engage.

name: Deep Squat (Malasana)

execution.note: Hold the bottom position to maximize the stretch.

instructions: Step 1: Stand with feet slightly wider than hip-width apart, toes turned out.
Step 2: Lower your hips down toward the floor into a deep squat.
Step 3: Keep your heels on the floor and your chest lifted.
Step 4: Place your elbows inside your knees to gently press them open.
Step 5: Rock gently side-to-side to find ease in the hips.

variations.name: 3-Minute Endurance Hold
variations.instruction_note: A static hold designed to build the mental and physical stamina needed for active labor.

variations.name: Casual Shifting (Daily Life)
variations.instruction_note: Perform this weight shift casually throughout the day, such as while brushing your teeth.

variations.name: Deep Squat to Hamstring Stretch
variations.instruction_note: From the squat, lift your hips toward the ceiling while keeping hands low to stretch the hamstrings.

variations.name: Low Squat Rocks
variations.instruction_note: Perform 10 rhythmic rocks in the deepest part of the squat to relax the pelvic floor.

safety_profile.trimester_3_notes: If your heels lift, place a rolled-up mat or towel under them. Use a yoga block for support if you have hemorrhoids or pelvic heaviness.
safety_profile.contraindications: Avoid deep unsupported squats if you have a known history of cervical insufficiency.

enrichment.benefits: Builds leg strength, stretches the inner thighs, and prepares the pelvic floor for the pressure of delivery.

name: Bear Hover

execution.note: Work up to holding for 60 seconds total.

instructions: Step 1: Start on all fours with toes tucked under.
Step 2: Take a big inhale to expand the belly.
Step 3: On the exhale, 'hug the baby' in and up towards your spine.
Step 4: Keeping that core engagement, lift your knees just 1 inch off the floor.
Step 5: Hold while maintaining a flat, table-top back.

variations.name: 3-Second Pulse Lift
variations.instruction_note: Instead of a long hold, perform repeated 3-second lifts with a full breath between each.

variations.name: Alternating Shoulder Tap
variations.instruction_note: While hovering, tap the opposite shoulder with your hand to increase stability challenge.

safety_profile.trimester_3_notes: This is an advanced move. Ensure you are 'hugging the baby' effectively to avoid straining the lower back.
safety_profile.contraindications: Stop immediately if you see 'coning' (a ridge forming down the center of your abs) or feel excessive pelvic pressure.

enrichment.benefits: Builds significant core and shoulder stability to help manage the weight of the third-trimester belly.

name: Asymmetric Rock Back
instructions: Step 1: Start on all fours.
Step 2: Place one knee on a yoga block or a thick book to elevate it.
Step 3: Keep your hands flat on the floor for stability.
Step 4: Slowly rock your hips back toward your heels and then forward again.
Step 5: Complete the set on one side, then switch the block to the other knee.

variations.name: Lizard Pose Deepen
variations.instruction_note: A more intense version of asymmetrical hip opening using a deep lunge position.

safety_profile.trimester_3_notes: Ensure the block is stable before putting weight on it. If this causes sharp pain in the front of the pelvis, stop and move to a symmetrical rock.
safety_profile.contraindications: Severe Symphysis Pubis Dysfunction (SPD) where uneven leg height causes pain.

enrichment.benefits: Uses an uneven pelvic position to help 'untwist' uterine ligaments and encourage the baby into an optimal head-down position.

name: Thoracic Reach & Rotate
instructions: Step 1: Start on all fours.
Step 2: Place one hand behind your head or reach it toward the ceiling.
Step 3: Rotate your chest and elbow/hand toward the ceiling.
Step 4: Rotate back down, tucking the moving arm under your chest toward the opposite side.
Step 5: Follow your hand with your eyes to ensure the movement comes from the upper back.

variations.name: Kneeling Lunge Rotation
variations.instruction_note: Perform the rotation while in a kneeling lunge position to add a hip flexor stretch.

variations.name: Low Lunge Thoracic Reach
variations.instruction_note: A dynamic version focused on reaching the arm high to maximize ribcage expansion.

safety_profile.trimester_3_notes: Avoid over-twisting the lower back; keep the focus on the upper spine and shoulders. If you feel dizzy, perform the movement more slowly or switch to a seated version.
safety_profile.contraindications: Sharp pain in the spine or ribs.

enrichment.benefits: Reduces upper back tension and increases the capacity of the ribcage to expand, helping with third-trimester shortness of breath.

name: Butterfly Pose (Rocking/Pulses)

execution.note: Stay upright to maintain space for the baby.

instructions: Step 1: Sit on the floor with the soles of your feet touching and knees out to the sides.
Step 2: Pull your feet as close to your body as is comfortable for your belly.
Step 3: Hold your ankles or feet and sit up tall.
Step 4: Gently rock your torso side-to-side or pulse your knees up and down.

variations.name: Butterfly Pulses
variations.instruction_note: Gently bounce the knees up and down like butterfly wings to loosen the hip sockets.

variations.name: Active Knee Press
variations.instruction_note: Use your hands or elbows to gently apply downward pressure on the knees for a deeper stretch.

safety_profile.trimester_3_notes: If sitting on the floor is uncomfortable, sit on a yoga block or a folded blanket to tilt the pelvis forward. Avoid leaning back too far.
safety_profile.contraindications: Sharp inner thigh or groin pain.

enrichment.benefits: Increases blood flow to the pelvic region and helps release the adductors, which can become tight as the body prepares for labor.

name: Quadruped Hip Shift
instructions: Step 1: Start on all fours with a neutral spine.
Step 2: Place one knee on a yoga block or a thick book to elevate it.
Step 3: Keep your hands and the opposite foot planted for stability.
Step 4: Lift the non-elevated hip toward the ceiling, then lower it toward the floor.
Step 5: Focus on the movement coming from the pelvis and hip, not the spine.

variations.name: Standing Hip Shift
variations.instruction_note: A standing version where you shift weight side-to-side in a forward fold to achieve similar pelvic mobility.

safety_profile.trimester_3_notes: Maintain a steady breath and avoid any sudden, jerky movements. Ensure the block is secure on your mat.
safety_profile.contraindications: Stop if you feel sharp pain in the pubic bone or have been diagnosed with severe Symphysis Pubis Dysfunction (SPD).

enrichment.benefits: Improves internal rotation of the hip, which helps open the pelvic outlet and supports the baby's descent during the second stage of labor.
